findings.claim: The 'keeps a plain Error whose message merely mentions eval' test uses a first-party stack, so it passes regardless of whether the EvalError type check is present, meaning the type check itself is not actually verified.
The 'keeps other reserved-name errors (TypeError, RangeError)' test also uses a first-party stack, so the stack check alone makes it pass without exercising the EvalError type condition.

If the 'errorEvent.error.type === "EvalError" &&' condition were removed from isCspBlockedEval, all five new tests would still pass, so the filter could silently drop every non-EvalError error from a third-party or stackless source without any test catching it.

The Error, TypeError, RangeError and undefined test cases should use a third-party stack (e.g. googletagmanager.com/gtm.js) or no stack at all, so that only the type check can cause them to be kept, properly covering the EvalError type condition.

The five new tests each add a '{} as any' context argument, increasing the file's total any-casts from 16 to 21, which conflicts with the project rule against using the any type or any type assertions.
The file already has a typed alternative pattern, 'const resourceContext = {} as RumEventDomainContext', that could be reused instead of the untyped any casts.

About 38 lines of comments surround two small predicates that are each only 2-3 lines long, which is excessive given the project convention that code comments should be treated as tech debt.
The comment mentioning 'grepped apps/web/src and packages/' is PR narration rather than lasting guidance and will go stale over time.
The comment stating 'We ship no eval()/Function() call of our own today' is PR narration rather than lasting guidance and will go stale over time.
The rationale for the filtering behavior is repeated three times across isNotFirstPartyStack, isCspBlockedEval, and the filterRumEvent JSDoc, which is redundant.
Nearby helper functions originatesFromExtension and isKnownNoise have no JSDoc at all, creating an inconsistency with the heavily commented predicates elsewhere in the file.

The comments should be reduced to a single short JSDoc on isCspBlockedEval covering what is dropped, the first-party exception, and WA-2952, with the dev/Cypress 'unsafe-eval' trade-off moved to the PR description instead of left in code.
